edges.description: TRAP is a long-established, though explicitly nonspecific, marker of bone disease, and its loss is followed by the characteristic failure to clear and replace cartilage during endochondral ossification. Whether TRAP acts as an effector of resorption here, rather than only marking it, is not established by the cited source.

edges.description: Sustained type I interferon exposure drives the lupus-like autoimmune spectrum, which is the commonest clinical problem in the disease.
intermediate_mechanisms: Interferon-driven loss of B- and T-cell tolerance, with autoantibody production.

evidence.reference_title: Tartrate-resistant acid phosphatase deficiency causes a bone dysplasia with autoimmunity and a type I interferon expression signature.
evidence.snippet: Sequencing of ACP5, encoding tartrate-resistant acid phosphatase, identified biallelic mutations in each of the cases studied, and in vivo testing confirmed a loss of expressed protein.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical, laboratory, and molecular characteristics of patients with spondyloenchondrodysplasia: a case series study.
evidence.snippet: The NM_001611.5 (ACP5): c.772_790del p.(Ser258TrpfsTer39) frameshift variant was identified in all patients.

nodes.description: Tartrate-resistant acid phosphatase is a lysosomal hydrolase expressed in cells of monocytic lineage, including osteoclasts and plasmacytoid dendritic cells. Null and missense ACP5 alleles both behave as nulls: plasma TRAP protein is negligible and the 5a isoform undetectable in patients, and the missense changes are predicted to destabilise the protein rather than merely reduce its catalytic rate.

evidence.reference_title: Tartrate-resistant acid phosphatase deficiency causes a bone dysplasia with autoimmunity and a type I interferon expression signature.
evidence.snippet: Compared to five age-matched controls, and an unaffected sibling to patients 2 and 3 who was homozygous for the wild-type allele on gene sequencing, levels of total TRAP protein were negligible, and TRAP 5a protein undetectable, indicating an almost complete lack of TRAP synthesis or secretion in the affected patients tested

evidence.reference_title: Spondyloenchondrodysplasia: An enigmatic immuno-osseus type I interferonopathy.
evidence.snippet: Type-5 acid phosphatase, also known as tartrate-resistant acid phosphatase (TRAP), is a lysosomal hydrolase expressed in cells of monocytic lineage, with activity against a wide variety of substrates

genetic_context.description: Biallelic ACP5 variants, including whole-gene deletion, nonsense, frameshift and missense alleles. The missense alleles behave as nulls rather than as partial-activity variants: plasma TRAP protein is negligible and the 5a isoform undetectable even in missense homozygotes, and the substitutions are predicted to destabilise the protein.

nodes.description: Elevated serum interferon alpha with upregulated interferon-stimulated gene expression in blood. This places SPENCD among the type I interferonopathies and explains why its autoimmune and neurological features resemble those of Aicardi-Goutieres syndrome and lupus rather than those of other skeletal dysplasias. The signature is not invariant: two mutation-positive patients in the largest survey did not show ISG upregulation, one of them while on immunosuppression.

evidence.reference_title: Spondyloenchondrodysplasia Due to Mutations in ACP5: A Comprehensive Survey.
evidence.snippet: In the majority of patients tested we detected upregulated expression of interferon-stimulated genes (ISGs), in keeping with the autoimmune phenotype and the likely immune-regulatory function of the deficient protein tartrate resistant acid phosphatase (TRAP).

evidence.reference_title: Spondyloenchondrodysplasia Due to Mutations in ACP5: A Comprehensive Survey.
evidence.snippet: Two mutation positive patients did not demonstrate an upregulation of ISGs, including one patient with significant autoimmune disease controlled by immunosuppressive therapy.

nodes.description: Reported in one patient with coexisting growth hormone deficiency, whose height improved from -3.0 to -2.35 standard deviations. This is a single-patient observation and does not establish growth hormone as a treatment for the skeletal dysplasia itself.

evidence.snippet: One patient had an associated growth hormone deficiency with fair response to growth hormone therapy (GH) where the height improved from -3.0 SD before GH therapy to -2.35 SD at presentation.

nodes.description: Immunomodulatory treatment directed at the autoimmune disease. Notably, the interferon signature normalised in one treated patient with significant autoimmune disease, which has been proposed as a marker of therapeutic response rather than merely of disease control.

nodes.description: Basal ganglia calcification with spasticity, and variably developmental delay, epilepsy and ataxia. In some families the neurological picture is severe enough to mask the skeletal and immune features and delay diagnosis until exome sequencing is performed.

evidence.reference_title: Spondyloenchondrodysplasia in five new patients: identification of three novel ACP5 variants with variable neurological presentations.
evidence.snippet: All our patients had spasticity with variable associations of motor and mental delay or epilepsy. All except for one patient had bilateral calcification in the basal ganglia.

evidence.reference_title: Spondyloenchondrodysplasia in five new patients: identification of three novel ACP5 variants with variable neurological presentations.
evidence.snippet: Such variable phenotypic presentations were masking the disease and led to the delay in diagnosis until exome sequencing was used revealing homozygous variants in the ACP5 gene as the cause of the patients' phenotype.

nodes.description: Janus kinase inhibition is the treatment that acts on the disease mechanism rather than around it: by blocking signalling downstream of the type I interferon receptor it targets the interferonopathy directly, and reported benefit is concentrated in the systemic autoimmune features. The evidence is a tabulated case series in a review rather than a trial, so the claim here is apparent efficacy, not established efficacy.

nodes.description: The skeletal lesion is a failure to clear chondroid tissue during ossification, leaving radiolucent islands of cartilage inside vertebral and metaphyseal bone. Those enchondroma-like lesions are what distinguish SPENCD from every other spondylometaphyseal dysplasia on a radiograph.

evidence.snippet: SPENCD can be differentiated from other spondylometaphyseal dysplasias by the presence of bone enchondromas which are radiographic radiolucent spondylar and metaphyseal lesions caused by persistence of chondroid tissue within the ossified bones

nodes.description: A broad autoimmune spectrum: systemic lupus erythematosus, autoimmune thrombocytopenia, autoimmune haemolytic anaemia, hypothyroidism, Sjogren syndrome, inflammatory myositis, Raynaud phenomenon and vitiligo. It affected 22 of 26 patients in the largest survey and is usually the presenting problem.
